svg.title: A cellular pair and relative homology
svg.desc: A curved cellular annulus K has both boundary circles as the gold subcomplex A. An oriented edge path gamma joins a on the inner circle to b on the outer circle. Its associated cellular one-chain c has boundary b minus a. A violet closed chain z and a teal face boundary show ordinary cycles and boundaries. The quotient map collapses all of A to one point, turning the composite path q composed with gamma into a loop. An overbar denotes a quotient chain; square brackets denote a homology class. The relative chain boundary is zero because both endpoints lie in A, while the connecting homomorphism sends the relative homology class of c to the class of b minus a in H zero of A. The chain module quotient and the topological quotient are distinct constructions.
svg.text: c is the cellular 1-chain of the edge path γ
q ∘ γ is a loop in K/A
the endpoints lie on different components of A
The relative differential and the connecting homomorphism have different codomains.
